phrases.notes: الْحِوَار (al-ḥiwār = the dialogue) + الثَّانِي (ath-thānī = the second).
مِنْ (from, pronounced with kasrah) + أَيْنَ (where) + أَنْتَ (masculine 'you')[cite: 3].
أَنَا (I) + مِنْ (from) + بَاكِسْتَان (Pakistan). In Arabic, the 'P' sound is rendered as 'B' (ب)[cite: 3].
هَلْ is a question tool placed before nominal sentences to form a Yes/No question[cite: 3]. بَاكِسْتَانِيٌّ uses the doubled Yā' al-Nisbah (ـِيٌّ) to form the nationality[cite: 3].
Subject pronoun أَنَا + nationality noun taking Yā' al-Nisbah[cite: 3].
مَا (what) + جِنْسِيَّتُكَ (your nationality, root جِنْس = origin/category + masculine suffix -ka) + أَنْتَ (emphatic pronoun)[cite: 3].
Masculine nationality ending in Yā' al-Nisbah (ـِيٌّ)[cite: 3].
A welcoming phrase conveying ease and familiarity[cite: 3].
